summary.text: Beth Van Duyne is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Texas's 24th District, first elected in 2020. Before Congress she served on the Irving City Council, as Mayor of Irving, and as the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development's Southwest regional administrator, and she also worked as a consultant. She serves on the Ways and Means Committee and chairs a Small Business subcommittee, and was unopposed in the 2026 Republican primary.

paragraphs.text: Lives in Irving, Texas, which her official biography says has been her home for over 30 years.
Earned a B.A. in city/regional planning and government and law from Cornell University, graduating magna cum laude according to her official biography.
Worked with startups, mid-size companies and Fortune 500 corporations and ran a consulting business, according to her official biography.

Served on the Irving City Council from 2004 to 2010, then as Mayor of Irving from 2011 to 2017; her official biography says she was the first woman elected mayor of the city. She won re-election as mayor in 2014, defeating Herbert A. Gears.

Was appointed in 2017 as Regional Administrator of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development's Southwest Region, overseeing HUD programs in Arkansas, Louisiana, New Mexico, Oklahoma and Texas under Secretary Ben Carson.
Is a former board member of the Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport, according to her official biography.

Won the open 24th District seat in the November 3, 2020 general election, defeating Democrat Candace Valenzuela and three others; she took office January 3, 2021 and succeeded Kenny Marchant. She was re-elected in 2022 with 59.7% (over Jan McDowell) and in 2024 with 60.3% (over Sam Eppler).

Serves on the Ways and Means Committee, with seats on its Oversight, Tax, Trade, and Work and Welfare subcommittees; chaired the Small Business Subcommittee on Oversight in the 118th Congress and chairs the Small Business Subcommittee on Economic Growth, Tax, and Capital Access in the 119th.

Was unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary, receiving 71,506 votes. Her official biography says she is the mother of two and was the second Republican woman from Texas elected to the U.S. House.
